faqs.q: Can you specify hose for a nacelle, pitch or yaw system by duty cycle rather than part number?
faqs.a: Yes, and it is the better enquiry. Send the flex life, minimum bend radius, temperature range and whether the assembly sits in the nacelle, hub or tower. A hose that meets the bore and pressure but fails the flex life becomes a service visit a hundred metres up, so we specify against the duty, add a flex-life and bend-radius statement where you ask for one, and say plainly when a catalogue compound will not survive the cycle.

faqs.q: Can a service kit be packed and tagged to one turbine's list before the crew leaves Esbjerg?
faqs.a: Yes. Send the turbine-specific list and we build every assembly to it, identify each one against its position and pack the kit as one unit. Offshore, the part is cheap and the vessel, the weather window and the technician time are not, so every assembly on the trip has to be right before departure. It is also worth adding anything marginal while somebody is already up there, rather than scheduling a second visit.

faqs.q: Is it worth paying more for a longer-lived hose than the turbine maker's original part?
faqs.a: Often, yes, for anything offshore or high in the tower. The assembly costs very little against the vessel day and technician time needed to change it, which inverts the usual economics: a construction with a longer flex life or a wider temperature range pays for itself if it saves one visit. Send the original part data and the duty, and we say where an upgrade is justified and where the original is already right.

faqs.q: Can goods go DAP to an Esbjerg offshore or wind base instead of stopping at the Aarhus quay?
faqs.a: Yes. Sea cargo lands at Aarhus and the short road leg to the Esbjerg base is priced with the order, not estimated afterwards. Give us the base, the consignee and any marking or packing rule the base operates, and the paperwork is prepared to match before the vessel sails. When a kit cannot wait for the sea lane, air freight into Copenhagen takes 2–4 days and continues by road.

faqs.q: Our site is on Zealand, near Kalundborg — does that change the port of entry?
faqs.a: It can. Aarhus suits Jutland and most Danish industry, including Fredericia; Copenhagen suits Zealand and the east, including the Kalundborg process estate. Clearance is identical at either port, so the choice is made on the inland leg alone. Tell us the delivery town when you ask for a quotation and we route the cargo to whichever port leaves the shorter road journey, then quote DAP to the site.

faqs.q: Does a full container for Aarhus go round the Skaw, or via Rotterdam like small orders?
faqs.a: A full container sails from Jebel Ali through Suez and round the Skaw to Aarhus, typically 26–32 days from dispatch. Small mixed orders travel as LCL, consolidated via Rotterdam and fed on to Denmark, which takes 32–40 days. When an order is close to filling a container, topping it up to take the full-container route can bring the date forward, and we say when that applies.

faqs.q: Is the PED declaration for a turbine assembly packed with the service kit or sent separately?
faqs.a: It travels with the goods. For a hose assembly above the pressure-volume threshold in PED 2014/68/EU, we issue the declaration of conformity as the assembler before dispatch and it accompanies the consignment, so a kit reaching Esbjerg carries its own paperwork. Below the threshold sound engineering practice applies and there is no mark. Pitch and yaw lines vary in bore and pressure, so we state which side each line falls on at quotation.

faqs.q: Our wind customer wants a flex-life statement — can it come with the REACH and origin documents?
faqs.a: Yes, in one set prepared before the vessel sails: the PED declaration of conformity for any assembly above threshold, the flex-life and bend-radius statement where the duty was specified, our REACH position on the elastomer compounds, and the Certificate of Origin, Dubai Chamber attested. The importer raises the EU customs entry into free circulation through Danish Customs on arrival at Aarhus or Copenhagen, and the goods then move on without another border.

faqs.q: Can piling-rig and excavator hose for the Fehmarnbelt works at Rødby go straight to the site?
faqs.a: Yes, on DAP terms to the site gate — excavator, crane and piling-rig hydraulics, with hose made up to length and fittings matched to the machine. For the tunnel works at Rødby or another Danish civil site, goods land at Copenhagen or Aarhus and the road leg is priced in the order rather than estimated. Send the machine make and model, or the old assembly's dimensions and end fittings, and we quote against them.

faqs.q: Can you supply jack-up and installation-vessel hydraulics for ships working from Esbjerg?
faqs.a: Yes — winch, crane, jacking and deck-machinery hydraulics, with hose made up to length and identified against the vessel's own line numbers where you send them. Goods go DAP to the vessel's base at Esbjerg, or to wherever the vessel is working if that is closer; for a project outside Denmark we often ship direct from Dubai rather than routing through a Danish address.

faqs.q: Which hose cover lasts in the dust around the Aalborg cement works and Danish quarries?
faqs.a: A dust-rated, high-cycle construction specified for the position — we supply cylinders, valves and hose assemblies for crushing, kiln-side handling and quarry plant, where dust and continuous duty shorten the life of a standard cover. Cargo for North Jutland lands at Aarhus and goes DAP to the plant. Tell us where each assembly runs and its working temperature, and we specify the cover and compound for that position rather than the pressure rating alone.

faqs.q: Do assemblies bound for Kiruna or Gällivare come with a low-temperature compound statement?
faqs.a: Yes, for anything going north. A standard nitrile stiffens well before the temperatures the northern mining belt works in, so a hose chosen on bore and pressure alone is the wrong hose by December. We specify a low-temperature compound, put it in writing at quotation, and say plainly when a catalogue item is unsuitable — a more useful answer than supplying exactly what was asked for.

faqs.q: How long does an order take to reach the mine gate at Kiruna or Gällivare?
faqs.a: Typically 34–42 days from dispatch: 28–34 days by sea from Jebel Ali through Suez to Gothenburg, then the long domestic road leg north. We quote it on DAP terms to the mine gate, with the road leg priced in the order rather than estimated. For a machine that is down, air freight into Stockholm Arlanda takes 2–4 days before the road journey north.

faqs.q: Can northern cargo come in through Luleå rather than being trucked up from Gothenburg?
faqs.a: In season, yes. Luleå serves the northern mining belt when the Gulf of Bothnia is open, and landing there shortens the road leg to Kiruna, Gällivare and the Norrbotten steel works considerably. Outside the season Gothenburg plus the road journey is the reliable route. Tell us the site and the date the goods are needed, and the quotation states which port and route it assumes.

faqs.q: Our plant is in Gävleborg or Västmanland — is an east-coast landing better than Gothenburg?
faqs.a: Often, yes, when the delivery sits on the east coast and the road leg from Gothenburg would cross the country. Gothenburg takes the direct sailing and serves the west and south, so it is the default for almost everything. For a plant around Stockholm, Västerås, Gävle or Sandviken, landing on the east coast shortens the inland leg. Tell us the delivery town and we route accordingly.

faqs.q: Our mine's supplier audit asks for material traceability — what can you provide?
faqs.a: Mill certificates traceable to heat number, where the contract requires them, issued by the mill or our test bench. The point is to confirm them at quotation rather than reconstruct them after an auditor asks, because a certificate tied to the actual heat has to be requested before the goods are picked. Tell us which lines need it and at what level, and we confirm what is obtainable before you order.

faqs.q: We are converting underground loaders to a fire-resistant fluid — what has to change on the hydraulics?
faqs.a: More than the fluid. Fire-resistant fluids carry less load and are harder on components than mineral oil, so seals, hose linings and sometimes permissible operating pressures change with them. A conversion that does not revisit what the fluid touches produces failures that look random and are not. Send the fluid designation with the existing hose specifications and we identify which assemblies and seals must change before the conversion, not after.

faqs.q: Do you supply hose for underground drill rigs and loaders working at depth?
faqs.a: Yes — high-pressure hose with abrasion-resistant covers, made up to length with fittings matched to the machine. Underground, a failed hose is a fire risk as well as a stoppage, so cover material, fluid compatibility and routing matter as much as the pressure rating. Send the machine, the fluid and the old assembly's dimensions and end fittings, and goods go DAP to the mine workshop.

faqs.q: We build machines in Sweden — do the hose assemblies we fit arrive with a PED declaration?
faqs.a: Where the assembly is above the pressure-volume threshold in PED 2014/68/EU, yes: we issue the declaration of conformity as the assembler and it travels with the goods. Below the threshold sound engineering practice applies and there is no mark. For a production build we state against each line which side of the threshold it falls on, so your own documentation is not left to guess.

faqs.q: Do you supply hydraulics for the new green-steel plant around Boden?
faqs.a: Yes, for new-build and commissioning work as well as spares — high-force cylinders, servo valves and heat-resistant hose built to the drawing. Cargo goes to Luleå in season or Gothenburg otherwise, then DAP to the site. The PED position is stated per line at quotation, mill certificates traceable to heat number are confirmed where the contract calls for them, and outdoor lines get a low-temperature compound.

faqs.q: Do intake-gate cylinders at a Norrland hydro station need a different hose for winter?
faqs.a: Usually, yes. Gate and intake assemblies sit outside or in unheated structures through a long northern winter, and a standard nitrile stiffens well above those temperatures. We specify a low-temperature compound for exposed lines and keep the catalogue default for those inside the powerhouse. Send the gate and governor line list with where each runs; for a planned outage, order early enough for the sea lane.

faqs.q: Why does a Finnish quotation say whether it assumes open water or ice?
faqs.a: Because between roughly December and April the Gulf of Bothnia ices over and the northern ports need ice-classed navigation, which adds cost and time. Open-water sailings to Helsinki run 30–38 days; in the ice season, northern ports run 36–48 days. A quotation raised in October for a February delivery is therefore not the same quotation, and we state the season it assumes rather than one band that is wrong for half the year.

faqs.q: What happens to a standard hose compound at minus thirty in Lapland?
faqs.a: It stiffens, the bend radius effectively grows, and a hose that passed inspection in September fails in January. A compound chosen for a Gulf summer is simply the wrong compound at that temperature. Tell us the working temperature range and we specify for it, with a low-temperature compound statement at quotation, or say plainly that the catalogue item is unsuitable.

faqs.q: Does the PED declaration also cover an assembly's low-temperature rating?
faqs.a: No — they answer different questions, so a winter order may need both. For a hose assembly above the pressure-volume threshold in PED 2014/68/EU, we issue the declaration of conformity as the assembler and it travels with the goods; below the threshold sound engineering practice applies and there is no mark. The low-temperature compound statement for the working range is a separate document, issued at quotation per duty.

faqs.q: How does cargo reach a Lapland mine such as Kittilä, Kevitsa or Kemi in midwinter?
faqs.a: On DAP terms to the mine or site gate, planned around the ice. Cargo lands at Oulu, subject to ice class in winter, or at Helsinki or Kotka, and the road leg north is long and seasonal, so it is quoted rather than estimated. Give us the site, the consignee and the working temperature, and both the compound and the delivery are planned for a Lapland winter.

faqs.q: Which Finnish port should our cargo use between December and April?
faqs.a: Name the delivery town and we will tell you, because in winter the choice narrows. Helsinki and Kotka take most cargo and serve southern industry; Rauma and Oulu serve the west coast and the north but need ice-classed vessels in the ice season. For a site near Oulu, a southern port plus the road leg is sometimes the better winter answer, and the quotation shows which route it assumed.

faqs.q: A line has stopped in February — should we fly a part into Helsinki rather than wait for an ice-class sailing?
faqs.a: More often than in other markets, yes. Air freight from Dubai into Helsinki takes 2–4 days, against 36–48 days by sea in the ice season, so the gap is at its widest here and for a stopped line it usually decides the question. For planned work, ordering against the season is the cheaper answer — send winter requirements before the ice closes the northern ports.

faqs.q: Why does one hose on our harvester crane keep failing while its neighbours last?
faqs.a: Usually routing, not hose quality. On articulating equipment a hose fails where it is constrained, not where it is loaded: a clamp that forces the bend at the fitting rather than along the free length destroys assemblies indefinitely, and a better hose changes nothing. Send photos and the assembly length; we check free length, bend position and clamping, and would rather solve the geometry than keep supplying replacements.

faqs.q: Do you supply hose assemblies to forestry machine builders around Tampere and Vieremä?
faqs.a: Yes — hose, fittings and assemblies for harvester and forwarder cranes, built to the builder's drawing and made up to length. A harvester crane flexes on every movement, so flex life and routing matter as much as pressure; we confirm both at quotation, specify the compound for minus-thirty working, and state the PED position per line for assemblies above threshold.

faqs.q: Can you supply hydraulics for icebreakers and ice-class vessels at the Turku, Rauma and Helsinki yards?
faqs.a: Yes — deck machinery, winch, crane and steering hydraulics, with hose made up to length and specified for sub-zero deck temperatures rather than the catalogue default. Yard deliveries go DAP to the shipyard gate. Send the line list, working temperature and end fittings; where the yard specification names a standard, tell us at quotation and we confirm line by line what we can evidence.

faqs.q: At Tornio or Raahe, can one machine need both a heat-resistant and a low-temperature hose?
faqs.a: Yes, and it is worth specifying per position. Lines near casting, rolling or furnace equipment need heat resistance, while lines on the same machine that run outdoors or in unheated bays see deep winter cold. One compound for both does one job badly. Tell us where each assembly runs and its temperature range, and cylinders, servo valves and hose go DAP to the works on one order.

One hose specified for the whole boat does one job adequately and the other badly. Split the list by where each assembly runs and we make them up to length, identified by position, on one consignment.

faqs.q: Which gate suits a delivery to Brno, and which to Ústí nad Labem?
faqs.a: Koper for Brno, Olomouc, Ostrava and the rest of Moravia — the sea leg out of Suez is much shorter and the road move up through Austria is straightforward, about 21–28 days in all. Hamburg and the Elbe rail corridor for Ústí, Prague and the north-west, about 27–35 days, where the inland leg reverses the advantage. We compare both against the delivery town on every quotation.

faqs.q: Is the PED declaration for a Czech order issued before or after the goods clear?
faqs.a: Before. Where an assembly is above the pressure-volume threshold in PED 2014/68/EU, we issue the declaration of conformity as the assembler before dispatch, and it travels with the goods to Koper or Hamburg, where the importer enters them into free circulation. Below the threshold sound engineering practice applies and there is no CE mark, so no declaration is issued for those lines.

faqs.q: What should go in the commissioning spares crate for a Czech-built machine?
faqs.a: The hoses most likely to be needed in the machine’s first year — usually the ones nobody thinks about while it is being built. Packing a small commissioning set with the machine costs little at that point and saves an air freight and a customs entry later, when the new installation is under scrutiny. Choosing the set is a short exercise on the schematic; send it and we quote the set.

faqs.q: Which fitting patterns do Czech machine builders order from you?
faqs.a: DIN metric, BSP, JIC and ORFS ranges, and GOST-pattern couplings where a machine is going to a market that specifies them, so one order can plumb the whole machine. Builders exporting plant usually need the destination market’s pattern rather than the one used at home, and we hold those ranges as stock. Send the drawing or the fitting list and we check each end against it.

faqs.q: Do you supply hydraulics for the lignite mines around Most and Bílina?
faqs.a: Yes — hose assemblies, fittings and valves for bucket-wheel excavators, spreaders, conveyors and dozers in open-cast lignite. That duty is abrasion, dust and frost before pressure, so cover material and cycle life lead the specification. For North Bohemia the Hamburg and Elbe corridor is often the better gate, and the quotation compares it with Koper.

faqs.q: Can you support maintenance at the Litvínov and Kralupy refineries?
faqs.a: Yes — industrial hose, hose assemblies, valves and fittings specified against the medium, temperature and pressure of each stream rather than a part number. Where a list is tied to a shutdown, sending it early lets it travel as one consignment through Hamburg or Koper, with air freight into Prague for late additions. The PED declaration is prepared where an assembly is above threshold.

faqs.q: Do you supply hydraulics for Czech hydro, pumped-storage and nuclear sites?
faqs.a: For governor, gate and actuator hydraulics on hydro and pumped-storage plant such as the Vltava cascade and Dlouhé Stráně, and for conventional-island equipment, yes. Any item a plant classifies as nuclear-safety related needs that plant’s own qualification; we confirm the document set at quotation and decline where we cannot evidence it.

faqs.q: Why do Ostrava and Třinec orders rarely go through Hamburg?
faqs.a: Because the arithmetic favours the Adriatic in the east of the country. Koper and road through Austria takes about 21–28 days from dispatch to Moravia-Silesia, while Hamburg and the Elbe corridor take 27–35 days and point at Prague and the north-west. When a line is down, air freight into Prague takes 2–4 days, with the road leg after it. These are typical transits, not delivery promises.

faqs.q: Can you supply press and clamping hydraulics for automotive plants around Mladá Boleslav and Kolín?
faqs.a: Yes — hose assemblies, fittings and valves for press, clamping and handling equipment in vehicle plants and their suppliers. On a production line the useful figure is cycle life at working pressure and the real bend radius, so tell us both. We can build and label assemblies as matched sets so a station is serviced in one intervention.

faqs.q: Do you supply hydraulics for river vessels and port cranes at Děčín and Mělník?
faqs.a: Yes — winch, hatch, steering and crane hydraulics for Elbe and Vltava barges and the cranes in the river ports. Equipment that works by the water through winter needs cover materials and compounds chosen for wet, cold duty. Send the vessel or crane model and the fitting ends, and these consignments usually come through Hamburg and the Elbe corridor.

faqs.q: What cycle data should a Slovak press shop send with a hose enquiry?
faqs.a: Cycles per hour, the working pressure, the bend radius the installation actually imposes and the planned service interval. A press line runs to a takt time, so the number to design against is cycle life rather than burst pressure. With those figures we issue a cycle-life statement against the line at quotation, or say plainly that a catalogue item will not reach the interval.

faqs.q: Can you quote a call-off against our line schedule instead of single orders?
faqs.a: Yes. Give us the consumption and the service interval and we quote a call-off with consignments timed to the planned maintenance windows, rather than a string of single orders. On a takt-time line the useful thing is predictability, not the lowest unit price. The 20–27 day lane via Koper sets how far ahead each call-off is released.

faqs.q: Can you label assemblies to our station list for planned replacement?
faqs.a: Yes. On a line running to takt, the cheapest hose is the one replaced in a planned window, which works only if the assemblies for a station arrive identified, interchangeable and complete. We build and label to your station list rather than to individual part numbers, so one intervention covers the station and nothing is matched up on the shop floor.

faqs.q: Do low-pressure return and pilot hoses on a press line need CE marking?
faqs.a: Not if the assembly falls below the pressure-volume threshold in PED 2014/68/EU — sound engineering practice applies and there is no mark. Higher-pressure assemblies above the threshold carry CE marking, with a declaration of conformity issued by us as the assembler that travels with the goods. A station set often contains both, and the quotation identifies each line.

faqs.q: When does Danube barge from Constanța make sense for Slovakia?
faqs.a: For project and heavy cargo — a large press component, a skid or oversized items that are awkward on the road. The barge runs from Constanța up the Danube to Bratislava in about 26–34 days in total. For line consumables Koper and road, at 20–27 days, is faster, and we say at quotation which suits the order.

faqs.q: Does a delivery to Košice or Žilina still come through Koper?
faqs.a: Koper is the default gate for Slovakia, with the road move up through Austria. Hamburg is used where the northern gate suits the delivery point better, and for eastern and northern Slovakia we compare the two against the town at quotation. Either way the goods clear once at the port, and the onward leg is domestic movement priced with the order on DAP terms.

faqs.q: Is it quicker to fly an urgent part into Vienna than into Bratislava?
faqs.a: Sometimes, because Vienna has more connections. Air freight runs from DXB to either Bratislava or Vienna, typically 2–4 days, followed by a short road leg — the two airports are about an hour apart. We book whichever gets the part to your line first, and the quotation names the routing.

faqs.q: Can you supply cylinder and servo-valve spares for the Košice rolling lines?
faqs.a: Yes — high-force cylinder spares, servo and proportional valves, hose assemblies and fittings for rolling, coating and finishing lines. Hot-mill duty adds radiant heat and scale to pressure, so we specify sleeving and covers to the position rather than the catalogue. Send the equipment, the valve or cylinder data plate and the circuit details with the enquiry.

faqs.q: Do you supply lock-gate and turbine-governor hydraulics for Gabčíkovo and the Váh plants?
faqs.a: Yes — hose assemblies, fittings and valves for lock-gate, sluice, governor and actuator circuits on the Danube barrage and the Váh hydro plants, specified for wet, cold and long-interval duty. Send the circuit pressure, fluid and the existing assembly markings, and we quote against them with sea freight via Koper or air freight into Bratislava when a unit is out of service.

faqs.q: Our Slovak company imports through Koper — who files the customs entry?
faqs.a: The importer, at Koper or Hamburg on arrival. Slovakia is inside the customs union, so goods are entered into free circulation once at the port and then move to Slovakia as domestic movement. Before dispatch we prepare the Dubai Chamber attested Certificate of Origin, the PED declaration for any assembly above threshold and our REACH position on the elastomer compounds.

faqs.q: What hose survives magnesite plant dust in the Gemer region?
faqs.a: Hose with an abrasion-resistant cover, routed and sleeved so it does not rub, because fine mineral dust wears the cover long before the pressure rating matters. Kiln and processing areas add heat. Tell us the position, temperature and cycle rate, and we specify dust-rated assemblies and fittings for magnesite, limestone and cement plant rather than standard workshop hose.

faqs.q: Why does most Austrian cargo come up from the Adriatic rather than down from Hamburg?
faqs.a: Because the Adriatic is materially shorter out of Suez. Sea and road via Koper or Trieste typically takes 20–26 days against 26–34 days through Hamburg and the Rhine corridor, and a container discharged at Koper is a few hours from Graz. We use the northern gate where the delivery sits in Upper Austria or Vorarlberg and the road leg reverses the advantage, and we choose against the delivery town rather than a forwarder’s default.

faqs.q: Does cargo cleared at Koper or Trieste need a transit document to cross into Austria?
faqs.a: No. Austria is inside the customs union, so the importer enters the goods once at Koper, Trieste or Hamburg into free circulation, and the road leg into Austria is domestic movement. There is no second entry at the border and no transit document. The consignment travels with our Dubai Chamber-attested Certificate of Origin, our REACH position on the elastomer compounds and, for assemblies above threshold, the PED declaration.

faqs.q: Can a CE-declared equivalent hose replace the original on an Austrian cable car or ropeway?
faqs.a: Usually not, and we will not propose one. On passenger-carrying equipment components are approved as part of a certified system, so an equivalent is not equivalent whatever its rating. Our PED declaration covers our own assemblies above the PED 2014/68/EU threshold; it does not transfer an approval. We source the originally specified part with its documentation, and where we cannot obtain it we say so rather than put a certificate at risk.

faqs.q: We build ropeways in Vorarlberg for resorts abroad — can you supply the specified hose to the export site?
faqs.a: Yes, where the specified part is one we can obtain with its documentation. Tell us the item exactly as it appears on the approved system and the destination; we quote DAP to the project site, FOB Jebel Ali or EXW Dubai for your forwarder, and confirm the document set at quotation. If the specified item is not available to us, we say so rather than offer a substitute.

faqs.q: Our site is in Tyrol — does flying a part into Vienna still beat the Adriatic lane?
faqs.a: For a stopped machine, usually yes. Air freight from Dubai to Vienna typically takes 2–4 days, and the onward road leg west is domestic movement priced with the order, so the total is still far shorter than the 20–26 day Adriatic lane. For planned maintenance in the west, the sea lane via Koper or the northern gate through Hamburg is the economical choice.

faqs.q: Can you deliver DAP to an Alpine valley station or a tunnel portal?
faqs.a: Yes. On DAP terms the road leg from Koper, Trieste or Hamburg to the site is domestic movement and is priced with the order. Tell us the exact delivery point and any access limits — weight restrictions, narrow approach roads, a seasonal pass — and we will say at quotation where the delivery needs a smaller vehicle than a standard trailer.

faqs.q: Do you supply hose and fittings for forging presses in Kapfenberg and Leoben?
faqs.a: Yes. Forging and rolling presses in Styria run high-force cylinders and servo valves, and the hose and fittings serving them are specified by working pressure, impulse duty and the fluid, including fire-resistant fluids near hot work. Send the press duty and the existing assembly data and we quote to it; material and test certificates come with the order where it calls for them.

faqs.q: Can hose near magnesite kilns in Styria and Carinthia cope with heat as well as dust?
faqs.a: Yes, if it is specified for both. Around magnesite kilns and sinter plant the hydraulics see radiant heat and fine abrasive dust together, so the cover, any heat sleeve and the fitting plating are chosen for where the line runs, not only for pressure. Tell us the machine, the distance from the hot zone and the cycle rate. The pits and the Erzberg haul fleet need dust-rated, high-cycle hose rather than heat protection.

faqs.q: What do you need to quote governor or gate hydraulics for an Alpine storage plant?
faqs.a: The plant’s existing assembly data — bore, length, end fittings, working pressure — and the fluid, plus any material certification the operator specifies, such as EN 10204 3.1. Governor, actuator and gate hydraulics on storage and pumped-storage schemes are often changed in a short outage window, so we confirm the full document set at quotation and dispatch everything for the window on one file.

faqs.q: Do you supply hydraulics for the aluminium plant at Ranshofen?
faqs.a: Yes. Extrusion presses, rolling stands and casting equipment at Ranshofen in Upper Austria use high-force cylinders, servo valves and hose that has to tolerate heat near the press and casting areas. Because Ranshofen sits in Upper Austria, we compare the northern gate through Hamburg with the Adriatic at quotation, and the road leg is priced with the order.

faqs.q: Why does a consignment to Switzerland carry two customs declarations?
faqs.a: Because Switzerland is surrounded by the EU customs union but outside it. A container discharged at Genoa or Rotterdam travels under EU transit bond — the T1, raised by the forwarder at the port of discharge — and the importer then makes a Swiss import declaration through the Federal Office for Customs at the border. It is the only European lane on our network that carries two customs files for the same goods.

faqs.q: What actually stops a truck at Chiasso or Basel?
faqs.a: A transit declaration and a Swiss entry that disagree on a description or a quantity. The sea leg to Genoa is predictable; the border is where a discrepancy surfaces, and it is a far more expensive place to resolve one than an office. We raise both declarations from the same invoice and packing list before the vessel sails, so the two files agree line for line.

faqs.q: When does a Swiss delivery come up the Rhine to Basel instead of over the Alps from Genoa?
faqs.a: When the site is in Basel or the north-west and the road leg is shorter that way. Genoa is the default — typically 24–32 days, sea and road combined, because it is much shorter out of Suez and the Alpine crossing is straightforward. Rotterdam and the Rhine corridor to Basel typically take 28–36 days, and we choose against the delivery town.

faqs.q: Does Switzerland accept a PED declaration, or is there a separate Swiss mark?
faqs.a: It accepts the European declaration: Switzerland recognises the European conformity framework for this equipment, so there is no separate national mark to obtain. For a hose assembly above the pressure-volume threshold in PED 2014/68/EU we issue the declaration of conformity as the assembler before dispatch, exactly as a member state would expect it. It travels with our Dubai Chamber-attested Certificate of Origin.

faqs.q: Can you supply to a tolerance tighter than the catalogue figure?

Swiss machinery and process plant often specify tighter than catalogues quote, and we would rather decline a line than ship to a nominal dimension. Material and test certificates come with the order where it calls for them.

faqs.q: How do you support planned hose changes on a tunnel boring machine underground?
faqs.a: By tagging and documenting each assembly against the machine list. A TBM cannot be pulled out for repair, so hoses are changed before they fail, in confined space and inside the excavation cycle. That only works if you know what is fitted, in what length and where on the machine. Send the machine list and we supply assemblies labelled to it, so the crew underground fits the right one first time.

faqs.q: Why does pumped-storage duty in the Valais wear hydraulics faster than a conventional dam?
faqs.a: Because the units change mode many times a day. A pumped-storage plant such as Nant de Drance switches between pumping and generating far more often than a conventional storage plant starts and stops, so governor, gate and valve hydraulics see many more pressure cycles. We specify hose and fittings for impulse life at that cycle count, from the plant’s existing assembly data, and confirm the document set at quotation.

faqs.q: Can hose for a Basel or Visp process plant be specified for the site’s cleaning regime?
faqs.a: Yes, and it should be. On chemical and pharmaceutical plant at Basel, Visp or Monthey a hose often fails from the cleaning cycle — hot caustic, steam or solvent flushes — rather than from the product. Tell us the product, the cleaning media, temperatures and frequency, and we confirm the lining and compound at quotation and say plainly where one is unsuitable. The document set for the line is confirmed at quotation too.

faqs.q: Can you supply steering and deck hydraulics for the passenger fleets on Swiss lakes?
faqs.a: Yes, to the vessel’s existing assembly data. Lake passenger fleets on Lake Geneva, Lake Lucerne and Lake Zurich run steering, ramp and deck hydraulics through long summer seasons, so overhaul spares are best ordered on the 24–32 day Genoa lane well before the season. For a breakdown in service, air freight into Zürich typically takes 2–4 days. Rhine barge and port-crane hydraulics for Basel are supplied the same way.

faqs.q: Do you supply hose for the salt mines at Bex and the Rhine saltworks?
faqs.a: Yes. Salt mining and brine handling attack hydraulics through corrosion as much as wear, so we specify covers, fittings and plating for a saline atmosphere and dust-rated, high-cycle duty on the mining fleet. Tell us the machine, where the line runs and the cycle rate, and we quote to that rather than to a standard catalogue assembly.

faqs.q: For a plant in Debrecen, is Constanța a better gate than Koper?
faqs.a: Often it is genuinely arguable, which is why we price both. Koper or Rijeka and road typically takes 21–28 days and is clearly best for Győr and the west; Constanța and the corridor west typically takes 24–32 days but shortens the road leg to Debrecen and the Great Plain. Hamburg is a third option. Whichever gate wins, the importer clears once into free circulation and the rest is domestic movement.

faqs.q: When does Danube barge from Constanța make sense for Hungarian cargo?
faqs.a: For heavy and project cargo, where the river changes the arithmetic. Sea to Constanța and barge upriver suits loads that are awkward or expensive by road. For line consumables and urgent spares, the Adriatic and road is faster, typically 21–28 days, and air into Budapest takes 2–4. We say at quotation which suits the order rather than defaulting to one.

faqs.q: What should a battery plant in Debrecen or Göd tell you about a dry-room hose line?
faqs.a: Which solvent is present, the humidity class of the room and whether the line serves a coating or electrolyte process. In a dry room a hose must be compatible with the solvent, must not carry moisture in and must not shed anything — constraints that rarely appear on a hydraulic specification. We specify against those conditions rather than against pressure alone, and say plainly where a compound is unsuitable.

faqs.q: How do you specify hose for a takt-time press line in Győr or Kecskemét?
faqs.a: From the cycles per hour and the planned service interval rather than the part number. On a takt-time line the cost of a failure is the stoppage, not the component, so impulse rating and fitting choice matter more than nominal pressure. Send the line duty and existing assembly data and we quote assemblies that last to your next planned stop.

faqs.q: Below the PED threshold, what paperwork comes with a hose assembly for a Hungarian plant?
faqs.a: No CE mark — below the pressure-volume threshold in PED 2014/68/EU sound engineering practice applies — but the consignment still carries our REACH position on the elastomer compounds, given at quotation, and a Dubai Chamber-attested Certificate of Origin. Above the threshold we issue the declaration of conformity as the assembler and it travels with the goods. The importer raises one EU entry at the port.

faqs.q: Which route do wellhead and valve orders for the Algyő field near Szeged take?
faqs.a: Whichever gate prices best to Szeged — we compare the Constanța corridor, typically 24–32 days, with Koper or Rijeka and road, typically 21–28 days. We supply TechnipFMC, Cameron (SLB), SPM, Anson, Stream-Flo and WOM equipment, plus industrial hose and flow lines for onshore production, and the document set the operator requires is confirmed at quotation. The importer clears once at the port of entry.

faqs.q: Do Hungarian consignments come through Rijeka as well as Koper?
faqs.a: Yes. Both are Adriatic gates for Hungary, typically 21–28 days from Jebel Ali, sea and road combined, and we pick between them by sailing and by the road leg to your town rather than by habit. Either way the importer enters the goods once into free circulation at the port and the run into Hungary is domestic movement. For Debrecen and the Great Plain, Constanța is priced as well.

faqs.q: What should Paks or the Mátra power station tell you before you quote conventional-plant hydraulics?
faqs.a: The qualification and documents the site requires, alongside the assembly data. For conventional plant — actuators, governors, turbine-hall and materials-handling hydraulics — we supply to the specification the plant issues, and at Visonta that includes the lignite handling fleet. We confirm the document set at quotation, and where a requirement is beyond what we can certify, we say so before you order rather than after.

faqs.q: Which hose compound can run on an NMP cathode-coating line at a Hungarian battery plant?
faqs.a: One specified against the solvent, not against pressure alone — tell us the solvent, its concentration and temperature, and whether the line enters the dry room. NMP and similar solvents attack materials that are stable elsewhere, so we confirm the compound and lining at quotation, give our REACH position on it, and say plainly if nothing we can supply is suitable rather than ship a near match.

faqs.q: Do you supply crane and hatch hydraulics for the Danube river ports at Csepel and Győr-Gönyű?
faqs.a: Yes — crane, hatch, winch and steering hydraulics for the river ports and the Danube barge fleet working them. Heavy project items for a port can travel by barge from Constanța, while urgent spares come faster by sea and road via Koper or Rijeka, typically 21–28 days, or by air into Budapest in 2–4.

faqs.q: Our cargo continues from Constanța to Moldova or Serbia — what changes?
faqs.a: The file does. A box continuing to Chișinău or Belgrade needs a transit declaration raised by the forwarder at Constanța before the onward leg, and that is set up from the outset. Retro-fitting one after the goods have been entered for Romanian free circulation is the expensive way round, so tell us the final destination at enquiry and we prepare the documents to match.

faqs.q: Does a modern CE-declared assembly fit Romanian plant built to a superseded standard?
faqs.a: Not automatically — the declaration covers conformity, not fit. For an assembly above the PED 2014/68/EU threshold our declaration of conformity travels with the goods, below it sound engineering practice applies, and every consignment carries our REACH position and a Dubai Chamber-attested Certificate of Origin. But older Ploiești or Midia plant may have ports to a since-replaced thread or seat, so send measurements and we confirm the mating ends before quoting.

faqs.q: Our old pump has a thread that looks standard but leaks with a new fitting — what should we send?
faqs.a: Measurements, not a cross-reference: the thread pitch, the seat angle and the sealing method taken from the component in hand. Much Romanian oilfield and refinery plant was built to standards since superseded, and a nominally identical thread can differ in pitch or seat, so a modern part engages and then leaks. We identify what actually mates with it, including where the honest answer is an adapter.

faqs.q: Can you supply wellhead and valve parts for mature onshore wells built to older API editions?
faqs.a: Yes, matched by measurement as well as by specification. Older wellheads around Ploiești and in the other onshore basins often carry connections from earlier API editions, so send nameplate data and dimensions with the enquiry. We supply TechnipFMC, Cameron (SLB), SPM, Anson, Stream-Flo and WOM equipment, and where a current part will not mate we say so and quote the adapter instead.

faqs.q: Can heavy spares for the Galați steelworks or the Iron Gates plant travel by Danube barge?

Sea to Constanța and Danube barge upriver typically takes 24–32 days, with Galați and Brăila handling the barge traffic, and it suits mill cylinders, large valves or turbine-hall items that are awkward by road. For containerised spares the sea lane to Constanța, typically 18–24 days, followed by road is faster, and we say at quotation which suits.

faqs.q: Does a plant in Timișoara, Cluj or Iași still receive goods through Constanța?

Constanța is the default port for Romania, typically 18–24 days by sea from Jebel Ali, and on DAP terms the road leg to Bucharest, Cluj, Timișoara, Iași or Arad is domestic movement priced with the order rather than left at the quay. For a stopped line anywhere in the country, air freight into Bucharest typically takes 2–4 days.

faqs.q: How do goods landed at Constanța reach the yards at Tulcea, Galați and Mangalia?
faqs.a: By road from the quay, or by barge for heavy items. Once the importer has entered the goods at Constanța, the run to Mangalia or Tulcea is a short domestic road leg priced with the order on DAP terms, and Galați and Brăila can also be reached by Danube barge for project cargo. Send the vessel equipment and existing assembly data for deck machinery, steering or crane hydraulics.

faqs.q: Do you supply hydraulics for track machines and rail works on the Romanian network?
faqs.a: Yes — hose, fittings and assemblies for tamping, ballast and track-renewal machines and for the cranes and excavators on rail and motorway contracts. These fleets are often a mix of Western and older Eastern-built machines, so send the machine make, model and the existing assembly data or measurements. Consignments land at Constanța and on DAP terms travel on to the depot or site by road.

faqs.q: Do you supply hydraulics for ship loaders and port cranes at Constanța’s grain and bulk terminals?
faqs.a: Yes — slewing, luffing and grab hydraulics for ship loaders, unloaders and port cranes, plus hose for the conveyors that feed them. Because these terminals sit at Constanța itself, a consignment can be delivered straight from the quay once the importer has entered it, typically 18–24 days from Jebel Ali. Send the crane or loader model and existing assembly data and we quote to it.

faqs.q: What hose do the Oltenia lignite mines need on bucket-wheel excavators and conveyors?
faqs.a: Dust-rated, high-cycle hose with abrasion-resistant covers and fittings that tolerate constant vibration and outdoor temperature swings. Bucket-wheel excavators, spreaders and conveyor drives around Rovinari and Motru run long duty hours in fine dust, and the cost of a failure is the stopped line. Tell us the machine, the line position and the temperature range, and we quote to that duty.

faqs.q: What should a Burgas refinery buyer send instead of a part number?
faqs.a: The medium, the temperature and the concentration. A compound that suits one hydrocarbon stream can be wrong for another at a different temperature, and at a refinery the failure is not a leak on a workshop floor. We issue a chemical compatibility statement for the named medium at quotation and say plainly where a compound is unsuitable, rather than supplying to bore and pressure and letting the plant discover it.

faqs.q: Is the PED declaration the same document as the chemical compatibility statement?
faqs.a: No — they answer different questions. The compatibility statement, issued by us at quotation per duty, says the compound suits your named medium. The declaration of conformity, issued by us as the assembler before dispatch, covers an assembly above the pressure-volume threshold in PED 2014/68/EU and travels with the goods. Below the threshold sound engineering practice applies and there is no mark, but the compatibility statement still applies.

faqs.q: Should we sleeve hose at the Pirdop smelter before it is due for change?
faqs.a: Yes — fit the sleeve before an incident rather than after. Around tilting furnaces and casting equipment the hazard is occasional contact with molten metal, which a standard cover does not resist. Silicone-coated fire sleeve does, chosen by the temperature and contact duration it must withstand. Tell us where each assembly runs and we supply it already sleeved, at Pirdop, the Plovdiv lead-zinc smelter or any furnace area.

faqs.q: Do the copper mines near Panagyurishte need different hose from the Pirdop smelter?

At the open-pit mines the hose on shovels, haul trucks and crushers fails from abrasive dust, vibration and long duty hours, so it is specified dust-rated and high-cycle. At the smelter the hazard is occasional contact with molten metal, so the assembly is fire-sleeved. Tell us where each line runs and we quote the right construction for each site.

faqs.q: Is the Maritsa East complex near Stara Zagora supplied through Burgas?

Burgas is the gate for the south, typically 18–24 days by sea from Jebel Ali, and on DAP terms the road leg to the Maritsa East mines around Radnevo and the power stations beside them is domestic movement priced with the order. Dust-rated hose for the mining fleet and governor and actuator hydraulics for the stations can travel on the same file.

faqs.q: Our refinery unit has changed its feed — do existing hose assemblies need re-specifying?
faqs.a: Possibly, and it is worth asking before the next change-out. A compound specified correctly for one hydrocarbon stream can be wrong for another at a different temperature or concentration. Send the new medium, temperature and concentration with the existing assembly data, and we issue a fresh chemical compatibility statement for the named medium, saying plainly if the current compound is no longer suitable.

faqs.q: Why can a small order to Sofia take longer than a full container to Burgas?

If an order is urgent, air freight into Sofia typically takes 2–4 days; if not, adding it to a larger consignment usually costs less than either.

We confirm the compound and lining at quotation for both chemical attack and abrasion, and Varna is the natural gate for these sites.

faqs.q: Is Limassol closer to Dubai by sea than most of North Africa?
faqs.a: In transit terms, yes. Full containers from Jebel Ali reach Limassol in typically 10–15 days, because nothing has to leave the Mediterranean after Suez, which makes Cyprus quicker than several of our North African lanes and our shortest route into the EU. Small mixed orders, consolidated with transhipment, take 16–24 days, so a full container is worth building where the order allows.

faqs.q: When does a consignment go to Larnaca instead of Limassol?
faqs.a: When a berth or a sailing at Larnaca suits the delivery better. Limassol is the default for almost everything, as the island’s container port and its ship management centre. Air freight from Dubai lands at Larnaca airport too, typically in 2–3 days, so an urgent item can be flown in while the rest of the order sails to Limassol.

faqs.q: Can you quote a complete spares set for an offshore campaign and take back what is not opened?
faqs.a: Yes. A drilling campaign is a fixed window with no practical resupply inside it, so the spares list should be built against what the equipment could need rather than what it probably will. We quote a campaign set on that basis, it ships before mobilisation, and we take back the unopened items afterwards. The return terms are agreed in the quotation, not after demobilisation.

faqs.q: Which specifications can you meet for offshore work in the Cyprus EEZ?
faqs.a: API-monogrammed assemblies, sour-service material documentation and flow-iron consumables, confirmed against the operator’s specification at quotation. We supply TechnipFMC, Cameron (SLB), SPM, Anson, Stream-Flo and WOM equipment, so wellhead, valve and flow-iron lines can sit on one quotation with the hydraulic hose. Name the API specification and any NACE MR0175 requirement on the enquiry so the certificates are priced in from the start.

faqs.q: Our Limassol-managed ships rarely call at Cyprus — how should their spares ship?
faqs.a: To your Limassol store, or onward on your forwarder’s booking, with the paperwork built for a ship rather than a plant. Each spare is bought against a class approval where the specification names one, so we confirm that at quotation, pack the certificate with the item and mark it to the vessel. When the part is fitted in another port months later, the surveyor sees the certificate with it.

faqs.q: If an assembly is below the PED threshold, what paperwork comes with it to Cyprus?
faqs.a: No CE mark, but not nothing. Below the pressure-volume threshold in PED 2014/68/EU, sound engineering practice applies and no declaration is issued; above it, our declaration of conformity travels with the goods. Every consignment carries a Dubai Chamber-attested Certificate of Origin, a manufacturer certificate of conformity is available on request, and any class approval is confirmed at quotation. The importer raises the EU entry through Cypriot Customs on arrival.

faqs.q: Can air freight into Larnaca catch a vessel leaving Limassol in two days?
faqs.a: Sometimes, and that is about the only case where it pays. Air from Dubai to Larnaca takes typically 2–3 days, against 10–15 days by sea to Limassol, so it is worth it for a single item a ship cannot sail without. For anything planned, the sea lane is short enough that air rarely repays the difference. Tell us the sailing time with the enquiry and we will say which works.

faqs.q: Do you supply the power stations at Vasilikos, Dhekelia and Moni?
faqs.a: Yes — actuator and governor hydraulics, hose assemblies, valves and fittings for thermal plant on an island grid, where a stopped unit has little margin. Cargo sails to Limassol and goes on by road on DAP terms, a short leg to each site. Send the equipment data plate or the original part numbers and we confirm the match at quotation rather than proposing an approximate equivalent.

faqs.q: Can spares for several managed vessels travel on one consignment, each marked separately?
faqs.a: Yes. A ship manager often has requisitions open for several ships at once, and one consignment to Limassol is cheaper than several. We pack and mark each vessel’s items separately, with their own certificates inside, and list them per vessel on the packing list, so your store can split the delivery without opening every box. Send the requisitions together and say which lines belong to which ship.

faqs.q: Do you supply crane and piling hydraulics for construction around Limassol and Nicosia?

Send the machine make and model, or the old assembly’s markings, and the fitting standard is matched in Dubai so the assembly fits on arrival rather than being reworked on site.

The sea leg to Rijeka or Koper is identical, but Serbia is outside the customs union, so the goods travel on under an EU transit declaration rather than entering free circulation, and a Serbian entry is made at Batrovci. That second file and the crossing are why the sea-and-road lane runs typically 22–30 days from dispatch.

faqs.q: What stops a truck at Batrovci, and how do you avoid it?
faqs.a: A mismatch between the two declarations. The EU transit declaration and the Serbian customs entry describe the same cargo, and a description or quantity that differs between them holds the truck at the border rather than at either customs office. We raise both from the same invoice and packing list before the vessel sails, so they agree line for line when the truck arrives.

faqs.q: Is industrial hose inside the scope of Serbia’s technical regulations?
faqs.a: Mostly not. Serbia applies technical regulations to a defined list, and much industrial hose and fittings sits outside it. Where a line does fall under a Serbian technical regulation, a conformity mark applies; it is arranged before shipment by an accredited body rather than discovered at the crossing, and the part list settles which lines are affected at quotation. A Dubai Chamber-attested Certificate of Origin travels with every consignment.

faqs.q: Is Thessaloniki and Corridor X ever the better gate for a Serbian delivery?
faqs.a: Yes, for southern Serbia it sometimes is. Sea to Thessaloniki and road north along Corridor X runs typically 24–32 days, against 22–30 through Rijeka or Koper and Batrovci. For Niš, Vranje or Kruševac the shorter road leg can outweigh the longer sea leg, so we compare both against the delivery town rather than defaulting to the Adriatic.

faqs.q: We run plant at Bor — will you quote to the mine gate, or only to Belgrade?
faqs.a: To the mine gate, on DAP terms. The road leg east from Belgrade to Bor or Majdanpek is quoted rather than estimated and priced with the order. For open-pit and concentrator duty we specify abrasion-resistant covers and high-cycle assemblies against the machine and the circuit, so tell us the shovel, truck or mill and the shift pattern rather than only the part number on the failed hose.

faqs.q: What wears out first on bucket-wheel excavators in the Kolubara and Kostolac basins?
faqs.a: Usually the hose cover, before the reinforcement. Lignite dust, constant slewing and outdoor winters wear the outside of an assembly faster than the pressure rating suggests. We supply abrasion-resistant hose to EN 856 and SAE J517, made up to length with the fittings the excavator, spreader or conveyor drive was built with, and we size the order around a planned overhaul rather than a single failure.

faqs.q: Our Smederevo line runs water-glycol fluid — which hose and seals suit it?
faqs.a: Ones rated for that fluid, which is not every hydraulic hose. Fire-resistant fluids are common near hot rolling and casting plant, and a tube or seal compound chosen for mineral oil can swell or harden in water-glycol or phosphate ester. Tell us the fluid type and working temperature with the bore and pressure, and we specify hose, fittings and servo-valve seals for that fluid rather than the catalogue default.

faqs.q: Can a Kragujevac automotive supplier have assemblies built to the carmaker’s drawing?
faqs.a: Yes. We make up hose assemblies to length in Dubai to your drawing — bore, end fittings, orientation and length between fitting faces — and tag each one with your part number. Material and test certificates come from the mill or our test bench where the order calls for them. If the drawing names a specific hose brand, say so at enquiry and we confirm whether we can supply exactly that.

faqs.q: Air feels safer for a landlocked plant — when is it a waste of money?
faqs.a: When it carries the routine lines. Air from Dubai to Belgrade takes typically 2–4 days and earns its cost on the assembly holding up production, not on the forty replenishment lines ordered with it, where it can multiply the freight for no operational benefit. Splitting by urgency — the critical item by air, the rest on the 22–30 day sea-and-road lane — is nearly always cheaper, and we price that split against the same line list.

faqs.q: Can barge operators on the Danube order winch and steering spares to the river port?
faqs.a: Yes. Hose assemblies, fittings, valves and cylinder seals for winches, steering, deck cranes and coupling gear on barges and pushers, and for the cranes at river ports in Belgrade, Novi Sad, Pančevo and Smederevo. Send the old assembly’s markings or the drawing, the working pressure and the fitting standard, and we deliver DAP to the port or yard.

faqs.q: Why do exact line descriptions matter so much on a Serbian order?
faqs.a: Because both customs files are built from them. The EU transit declaration and the Serbian entry are raised from our invoice and packing list, so a vague or inconsistent description at enquiry becomes a mismatch at Batrovci. Give us description, quantity, bore, end fittings and working pressure for each line, plus the delivery town and importer of record. NACE MR0175 / ISO 15156 material documentation is supplied where the contract requires it, with material and test certificates from the mill or our test bench, and it travels to Durrës with the goods and the Dubai Chamber-attested Certificate of Origin. Mark the sour-service lines on your enquiry.

faqs.q: Do Albanian imports clear in one step, or through a neighbour first?
faqs.a: In one step. Albania is outside the EU customs union but has its own port, so the importer makes a single entry through the General Directorate of Customs at Durrës, rather than inheriting a transit from a neighbour plus a border declaration. There is no blanket pre-shipment conformity scheme for industrial hose and fittings; what travels with the goods is the material documentation the field asks for.

faqs.q: Why does cargo for Durrës tranship rather than sail direct?
faqs.a: Because Durrës does not take a mainline call from the Gulf. Cargo from Jebel Ali tranships in the Mediterranean and waits for a feeder up the Adriatic, which is why a full container takes typically 20–28 days. We build the consignment around the connection and send the paperwork and tracking together.

faqs.q: How do goods get from the quay at Durrës to a wellsite near Patos?
faqs.a: By road, on DAP terms to the field or the base at Patos or Fier. The road leg south from Durrës is short and it is priced with the order. For the southern fields, Vlorë can be the better port of discharge, and we compare it with Durrës at quotation.

faqs.q: Do you carry spares for the older wellheads on Albania’s onshore fields?
faqs.a: Often, if we can identify the equipment. Send the make, the API 6A size and pressure class, and the nameplate or part number, and we quote valves, chokes, seal kits and flow iron to match, alongside the hose and fittings on the same consignment. We supply TechnipFMC, Cameron (SLB), SPM, Anson, Stream-Flo and WOM equipment, with material and sour-service documentation where the field specification calls for it.

faqs.q: Our machine came second-hand without a parts list — how do we identify a fitting?
faqs.a: Measure it rather than describe it. Across the flats of the hex, the outside diameter of the thread, whether the seat is cone or flat, and the overall length between end faces identify most fittings unambiguously. Send those four numbers and a photograph, and we match the connection — metric, BSP, JIC or NPT — and quote a complete assembly made up to length.

faqs.q: Why does a small mixed order to Durrës take up to 36 days?
faqs.a: Because it travels consolidated, with two transhipments. LCL from Jebel Ali to Durrës runs typically 26–36 days, against 20–28 for a full container, since the consolidated cargo waits at each transfer. For a few cartons that is still usually the economical answer; for a single urgent item, air into Tirana takes typically 3–5 days.

faqs.q: Which lifting gear is worth sending with a workover package for Patos-Marinza?
faqs.a: The slings, shackles, hooks and master links the rig-up plan actually names, sized to its working load limits. We supply wire rope and chain slings and lifting accessories marked with their working load limit and with the manufacturer’s test certificates the order calls for, listed on the same invoice and packing list as the oilfield lines. We confirm the document set at quotation; examination on site stays with your appointed lifting inspector.

faqs.q: Do you supply drill and hoist hydraulics for the chrome mines around Bulqizë?
faqs.a: Yes. Hose assemblies with abrasion-resistant covers, fittings, valves and cylinder seals for drills, loaders, hoists and crushers in chrome mining, made up to length and pressure-tested in Dubai. Send the machine, circuit and working pressure; delivery is DAP to the mine or a yard in Tirana or Durrës.

faqs.q: For a Kosovo delivery, does Durrës or Thessaloniki land cheaper?
faqs.a: It depends on the delivery town, which is unusual. The Durrës corridor east through Vërmicë and the Thessaloniki corridor north both run typically 22–30 days and are close in cost, so Prizren and Gjakova usually lean west while Ferizaj and Gjilan lean south. We price both on every order rather than defaulting to one, because the difference is a real share of the landed cost.

faqs.q: How is a delivery to Trepça or the Obiliq stations priced and cleared?
faqs.a: Priced DAP to the mine or plant gate, with the short road leg from Pristina included in the order. It is cleared on two declarations — the transit declaration raised by the forwarder and the Kosovo customs entry — built from the same invoice and packing list, so they agree line for line at the crossing and the truck is not held there.

faqs.q: Which hose holds up on lignite conveyors, crushers and stacker-reclaimers?
faqs.a: Hose with an abrasion-resistant cover in a dust-rated assembly. Lignite dust and continuous running wear the outside of a hose long before the pressure rating is reached, especially on conveyor drives, crushers and stacker-reclaimers. Tell us the duty, not only the part number, and we specify spiral hose to EN 856 or SAE J517, made up to length with the fittings the machine was built with.

faqs.q: On a mine that never stops, which spares should we hold?
faqs.a: The few assemblies whose failure stops everything downstream. On continuous excavation and conveying, one hose can hold up a whole production chain, so its value is not its price. Following the process rather than the equipment list identifies those items, and the list is usually shorter than expected. We work through it with you and quote the critical spares as one consignment.

faqs.q: Can critical spares for the Obiliq stations be packed as one kit per machine?
faqs.a: Yes. Once the critical list is agreed, each assembly is made up to length, pressure-tested in Dubai and tagged with the machine and its position on it, then packed by machine rather than by part number. A shift crew changing a hose on a conveyor drive or stacker-reclaimer then finds the right assembly without searching a mixed crate. The kits travel on one transit declaration to the plant gate.

faqs.q: What does Kosovo Customs need to see when the truck reaches the border?
faqs.a: A Kosovo customs import declaration, lodged by the importer, that matches the transit declaration raised by the forwarder at Durrës or Thessaloniki line for line, with a Dubai Chamber-attested Certificate of Origin and any material and test certificates the specification calls for. There is no blanket pre-shipment conformity scheme for industrial hose and fittings; what has to be right is that the two declarations agree.

faqs.q: A Trepça hoist is down — should the replacement fly or wait for the road?
faqs.a: Fly the part that stopped the hoist, and send the rest by road. Air from Dubai into Pristina takes typically 3–5 days with a connection, against 22–30 days by sea and road, so it pays on the critical assembly, not on routine lines. Send the old hose’s layline, end fittings and length between fitting faces, and we build and pressure-test the assembly in Dubai before it flies.

faqs.q: Can workshops in Mitrovica or Pristina order bulk hose and loose fittings to crimp themselves?
faqs.a: Yes. Bulk hose on the reel, with matching ferrules and fittings from the same maker’s system, ships alongside finished assemblies, so a workshop rebuilding mining or construction machinery can crimp its own. Mixing hose and fittings from different systems is the common cause of a crimp that fails, so tell us the crimper and die set you use and we match the components to it.

faqs.q: What do you need from us to price both corridors for a Kosovo order?
faqs.a: The delivery town, the line list and the importer of record. With those we price Durrës–Vërmicë and Thessaloniki routings side by side, on DAP to your site, CIF Durrës, FOB Jebel Ali or EXW Dubai for your nominated forwarder. For each line give the bore, end fittings and working pressure, and the quotation comes back in EUR.

faqs.q: Do you build to EN 853 for our European machines and SAE J517 for the American ones?
faqs.a: Yes — we build to whichever standard the machine was designed around. European excavators usually take EN 853 or EN 856 hose with metric DIN 24° cone or BSP ends, while American trucks and loaders run SAE J517 hose with JIC or ORFS ends, and one order can cover both. Tell us the standard and end connection for each line, and assemblies are made up to length and pressure-tested in Dubai.
